findings.failure_path: A tool discovered during a loop must become callable at the next model invocation, which necessarily changes that loop's tool definitions, while llm-client-gateway.md simultaneously says never to add or remove definitions mid-loop. Following the gateway leaves the discovered tool unreachable; following dispatch invalidates the tools-first cache prefix. Appending its schema after the last cache breakpoint is also incompatible with the documented tools-before-system/messages ordering when that breakpoint is later in the prompt.
findings.smallest_fix: Define one boundary consistently: forbid mutation only during an in-flight invocation, and either start a new cache generation and accept the prefix miss when adding a schema between invocations, or predeclare schemas and change only masked availability. Remove the suffix-only cache claim for providers whose tool block is at the prefix head.

challenge_focus: Fresh full adversarial pass on the post-fix candidate (not a confirm-my-fixes pass): (1) the mandatory-invalidation clause against the compaction and cache-attribution rules — a path where a generation reset is skipped or a revoked item survives; (2) the next-model-invocation boundary for discovered tools — a mid-loop tool still unreachable, or an evicted tool still cited; (3) the trifecta edge-cutting test — a pattern that passes the wording while injected text still reaches an exfiltrating action; (4) the OWASP supply-chain and poisoning checks — enforceable or still declarative; (5) the delegation fan-out gate, effort_budget field, artifact-not-relay line, MAST classification, and topology default — bypass-by-omission, and over-broad cost on a simple single-agent delivery; (6) register rows and firing paths — moved anchors, claims the receipts do not support; (7) vendor numbers as invariants, attribution errors, private-path or organization-noun leakage.
